dedupe_keys.name: citizen science food price survey for newfoundland and labrador including remote nunatsiavut communities 2020 2021

description: This workbook records what shoppers actually paid for staple foods in stores across Newfoundland and Labrador, including fly-in and coastal Inuit communities where food must travel long distances and is subsidised. The producers are Max Liboiron, Morgan Davidson, Kaitlyn Hawkins and other volunteers and researchers with the Civic Laboratory for Environmental Action Research at Memorial University of Newfoundland. Coverage is about 4,700 price checks from October 2020 to December 2021, collected every two weeks in some places and once in others, in communities such as Rigolet in Nunatsiavut as well as larger towns. Each row gives the date, place and health region with coordinates, the store, the item and whether it is essential, whether it falls under the Nutrition North Canada subsidy, price, size, unit price, sale price, whether it was on the shelf and whether it was bought in person or online. The workbook is available as a free download from Zenodo under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence, and a report explains the findings. Caveats: volunteer sampling with uneven timing and places, and a limited basket of items. Simulation uses: modelling food affordability and shortages in remote supply chains that depend on air and sea transport. Related records: the WFP global food prices (data-wfp-global-food-prices) give market prices in other regions.
